Quantum Systems a Air Land Maritime Multi Domain Neo-Prime
Quantum Systems is a European defence neo-prime developing autonomous systems for defence, security and civil resilience. We bring hardware, software and AI together
across air, land and sea – helping democracies and their allies turn technological advantage into operational capability.
We do this in 5 points that define who we are as Quantum Systems.
Changing how defence capability is built
We challenge established development cycles by connecting operational experience directly with engineering. Our teams turn real-world requirements into autonomous capabilities that can be improved, integrated and delivered at scale.
Our purpose is to strengthen the ability of democracies and their allies to protect their people and
Our technology combines unmanned platforms and sensors with software, AI and mission integration. That depth allows us to develop the physical system and the intelligence that makes it useful together. Operational feedback informs improvements across the technology stack, while open integration connects our capabilities with partner systems.
HARDWARE – Unmanned platforms and sensors
Software– Mission management and system integration
AI – Autonomy, data interpretation and decision support
We bring unmanned systems across domains into a connected operational network. MOSAIC UXS provides the software backbone, integrating platforms,
sensors and partner technologies so customers can build capability around their mission.
Extend mission awareness with unmanned aerial systems and airborne sensing, connecting intelligence from above to the wider operational picture.
Bring unmanned systems and autonomy to ground operations, connecting mobile platforms and sensors to support the mission across complex terrain.
Connect unmanned systems above and below the surface, bringing maritime sensing and autonomous capabilities into the wider operational network.
THE SOFTWARE BACKBONE Connect platforms, sensors and operators across domains through a shared software backbone, bringing distributed information into one operational picture.
